correctness.summary: The expectation proof sandwiches the repeat deficit between two renewal sums of block surprisal. Bounded renewal overshoot gives t/H+O(1), while a direct periodicity calculation bounds every overlapping-repeat probability by p_max^k, making overlap corrections summable. Bounded-increment Hoeffding estimates then give the two one-sided bounds needed for L1 convergence. A deterministic-seed suffix-automaton simulation supplies supplementary numerical checks.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The uniform-source first correction is prior art: Janson, Lonardi and Szpankowski (2004) prove a sharper expansion for unbiased memoryless sources. Ahmadi and Ward (2020) and Gheorghiciuc and Ward (2007) study fixed-length k-subword complexity, including nonuniform sources. The claim is restricted to the all-length nonuniform i.i.d. correction n log n/H with O(n) remainder, its L1 law, and the overlap-robust renewal proof. Older sources under different terminology, especially Ivanko (2008) and the complete Dębowski chapter, remain residual risks because they were not fully inspected.

value.summary: The result replaces alphabet-size scaling by the exact inverse-Shannon-entropy coefficient for arbitrary fixed nonuniform i.i.d. sources and adds first-correction-scale L1 concentration, clarifying how the typical surprisal threshold controls total distinct-substring complexity despite window overlap.

limitations: At least two positive-probability symbols are required.
No refinement of the O(n) expectation remainder is proved.
No variance asymptotic or limiting fluctuation law is identified.
The full 2008 Ivanko article and the complete Dębowski chapter were not fully inspected.
Independent audit has not been performed.
